narratives.Description: Small changes pay the same lifecycle ceremony as large ones: a full brief, narratives and clause scaffolding, whatever the size of the diff. This story adds a small-change lane under the rapid ceremony dial: a measured, fail-closed bound on the change, a thin command-backed brief that the existing gates admit, and a lane exit that converts the scope to the full brief shape when the bound is crossed. Multi-PR relief (P2) stays with #6203 and #680.

narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer making a small change under the rapid dial, I want a thin brief whose acceptance is its commands, admitted by preflight, verify:ac and scope:complete, so that the ceremony scales with the change and a change that grows past the bound is moved to the full shape instead of slipping through.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Follow the accepted Prefer-A Bound on #6204 (comment 6811591036). Add a small-change evaluator next to the ceremony dial policy (packages/core/src/policy/) that measures cumulative production-file and changed-line counts against the lane-admit base, rechecks at every gate that can refuse, and refuses on an unknown public surface. Add a thin-brief emitter that writes only title, issue ref, file_scope and acceptance commands inside xBRIEF 0.8, and only when command-backed acceptance already exists. Make preflight, verify:ac and scope:complete admit that thin shape without narrative, plan or clause scaffolding, with delivery identity unchanged. Add the lane exit: once the bound is crossed, refuse on every retry until the full brief shape passes, as a scope-local conversion distinct from the #3319 dial raise. N/M bound defaults are policy values; a new numeric constant needs a human intent-constraint mint. Cover each limb with focused vitest cases and add a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.

## Plain-language summary
Today the ceremony dial can lighten session ritual and check depth, but a tiny fix still gets a fat brief and a multi-PR lifecycle. This draft picks one Prefer-A: under rapid, when a hard small-change bound holds, emit a thin brief and ride one PR; if the change grows past the bound, refuse once and tell the agent to escalate to the full shape.

## Bound remedy
- Small-change predicate under rapid — Admit the lane only when ceremony dial depth is rapid and a typed bound holds (production file count, changed-line count, and no new public surface). Bound lives next to ceremonyDial policy; one fail-closed evaluator. relieves: P1, P2
- Minimal brief shape — Emitter writes title, issue ref, file_scope, and acceptance commands only. That shape MUST pass xbrief:preflight, verify:ac, and scope:complete without narrative/plan/clause scaffolding. Delivery identity (#3041 / #3675) unchanged. relieves: P1, P4
- One-PR compose — Product + brief (+ completion when #680 path exists) land in one PR via the #6203 forge-attested human-approval admit. Without a qualifying approval, Path B brief-first behaviour is unchanged. relieves: P2
- Mid-flight escalate-once — When the bound is crossed after admit, one refuse with one remediation that names escalate-to-full-shape (same two-stage spirit as vbrief.md ceremony dial). No silent keep-minimal. relieves: P3

## Reject list (draft)
- Soft / advisory-only small-change hints that agents may ignore
- A second parallel brief schema outside xBRIEF 0.8
- Weakening delivery identity or AC verification to make the thin brief green
- Shipping one-PR by relaxing merge-base scope-provenance without the #6203 approval proof
- Auto-ingest or primary mutation from this arc

## Footnotes (non-mechanism)
- Naming: small-change lane / rapid-small; docs and strategy pointers are footnotes unless they change the fail-closed association (#5783 / #3368).
- Ship order with #6203 / #680 is composition, not a second Prefer-A mechanism.

Round-1 refutation of Prefer-A remint https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/6204#issuecomment-6811408519
Envelope ceiling: 6811411309 (inclusive). Pin: e514bc81132ff8c3bfbb5f9cdf6490d80bfcdc5a. audit-targets: none.

The thin brief is plausible, but the admission and acceptance contracts are not yet sufficient to bind this exact remedy.

### C1 — blocks-the-design — A typed bound needs an authoritative measurement contract
Evidence: the remint requires production-file count, changed-line count and no new public surface, but supplies no comparison baseline, measured artifact, public-surface oracle or unknown-result rule. At the pin, `packages/core/src/policy/ceremony-dial.ts` explicitly calls `estimateProvisionalCeremonyInputs` provisional: it accepts file counts, environment and prompt signals; `ceremonyDialProfile` scales cold ceremony, not verification. Those existing signals cannot certify the new hard bound.
Failure mode: an agent admits an empty worktree, adds a new exported command in one line, and retains minimal status using the initial count or a self-declared no-public-surface flag. A last-commit count also admits an oversized cumulative change split across commits. This is an authority/input-trust issue, not merely threshold tuning.
Consequence: before bind, name the cumulative product diff and comparison base, when the same predicate is rechecked, and an authoritative supported public-surface determination (unknown refuses/escalates). Keep one evaluator; do not turn the provisional dial estimator into proof. Numerical N/M defaults can remain implementation detail.

### C2 — blocks-the-design — Command-only eligibility leaves valid small changes without their acceptance oracle
Evidence: the remint says title, issue ref, file_scope and acceptance commands **only**, while promising unchanged AC verification and no clause scaffolding. At the pin, `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts` has a separate no-stated-command path: `stampDerivedClausesOnAcceptance` derives clauses from the task statement, `collectPlanItemAcceptanceSurface` and `collectDeclaredAcceptanceNarrativeSurface`; `readAcceptanceClauses` reads persisted clauses. These are meaningful acceptance sources, not universally disposable boilerplate.
Failure mode: a tiny fix has behavioral acceptance prose but no operator-stated command. Removing both the declared sources and derived clauses either loses that acceptance obligation or leaves the thin brief unable to satisfy the existing verifier. Inventing a generic test command is not proof that the original behavior was preserved.
Consequence: restrict this first lane to briefs with a valid supported command-based acceptance record, falling back to the full shape otherwise; alternatively preserve the existing derived acceptance representation. Do not promise command-only shape for every size-qualified change. Keep the xBRIEF envelope and native issue/file-scope locations so existing delivery identity readers still operate.

### C3 — sharpens-framing — Escalate once must mean one remediation, not one lifetime refusal
Evidence: `packages/core/src/policy/ceremony-dial-escalation.ts` says `evaluateCeremonyDialEscalation` does not persist a transition. `escalateCeremonyDial` in `ceremony-dial.ts` changes policy for future session starts. Neither operation expands the current brief. The remint currently says one refuse with one remediation, without defining successful exit from refusal.
Failure mode: the agent runs the existing dial escalation, retries in another session, and mistakes a changed depth or a previously emitted warning for a converted brief. A shared policy change could also affect another worker's unrelated small scope.
Consequence: clarify that the current scope remains refused on every retry until its full representation passes the existing gates; once describes the remediation vocabulary, not a bypass after the first failure. Conversion preserves scope identity and AC evidence and is scope-local. This sharpens the stated no-silent-keep-minimal intent rather than adding another mechanism.

### C4 — sharpens-framing — P2 is contingent, not presently relieved

metadata.issueBody:
## Problem

The ceremony dial (#3214) scales session ritual and check depth. It does not scale the lifecycle. A 14-line fix still gets a full brief (often ~200 lines of JSON), its own activation PR, and its own completion PR. Lifecycle JSON in one consumer run nearly equalled product lines.

## Proposal

When the dial selects `rapid` and the change is small (define the bound: for example, at most N production files and M changed lines, and no new public surface):

- Brief: emit a minimal shape (title, issue ref, `file_scope`, acceptance commands). Omit narratives, plan items and clause scaffolding that only exist for larger scopes.
- PR count: one PR. Uses the one-PR path from #6203 and the completion path from #680.
- Escalate to the full shape when the change grows past the bound, like the dial's two-stage path in `vbrief.md`.

## Acceptance

- A small change under `rapid` produces a minimal brief that passes `xbrief:preflight`, `verify:ac` and `scope:complete`.
- A change that crosses the bound mid-flight is told to escalate, once, with one remediation.
- Delivery identity (#3041 / #3675) and AC verification stay unchanged.

## Related

#3214 (dial), #680 (completion PR), #5931 (tiny-PR review ceremony), #3813 (ceremony economy), #3631 / #4012 (chore and lifecycle-only CI lanes).

expected_outputs: measured small-change bound evaluator next to the ceremony dial
preflight / verify:ac / scope:complete admit the thin shape
lane exit: refuse until the full shape passes
swarm.acceptance_criteria_justification: Four clauses map one-to-one to the four limbs of the accepted Prefer-A Bound; the bound, the thin brief and the lane exit share one evaluator, so splitting them would ship an unbounded thin brief.
